chunks: So, when you clash with the unbelievers, smite their necks until you overpower them, then hold them in bondage. Then either free them graciously or after taking a ransom, until war shall have come to end.
That is it. If God had pleased He could have punished them (Himself), but He wills to test some of you through some others.
He will not allow the deeds of those who are killed in the cause of God to go waste.

key_terms.ضَرْبَ الرِّقَابِ: smiting the necks (decisive strike in battle)

ai.seo_question: What are the stages of handling captives and the theological reason for war in this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: Known as the 'Verse of the Sword' (Āyat al-Sayf), this passage establishes the legal framework for jihad, transitioning from the initial phase of combat to the management of prisoners of war. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Ayyashi and Al-Qummi, emphasize the context of its revelation during the Battle of Badr or Hunayn, highlighting the strategic shift from active engagement to securing peace. The verse underscores divine wisdom in testing the faithful through mutual conflict, while guaranteeing that the sacrifices of martyrs are preserved and rewarded.
